$comment: Standing platform test checklist — area ledger. Hand-edited, append-only; validated by scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs (pnpm check:platform-checklist). Authoring rules: docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md · execution protocol: RUNNER.md.
title: Cross-cutting UX conventions — every write answers, every disabled control explains itself, labels over machine names (console and Studio)

items.title: Every user-initiated write answers visibly — success names what changed, a refusal says why, and a no-op claims nothing
personas: member (non-admin end user) for the record rows

requires: a writable scratch package for the Studio rows — create it from the Studio landing and delete it at teardown; the showcase package itself is read-only in Studio
the organization capability for the Invite User row (a stock showcase boot bootstraps a Default Organization)
an independent read of server truth for every row — a second browser context or the REST API — so a write is never judged by what the UI says about it
knownGaps: Expected FAIL on stock: Setup → Users → Invite User declares successMessage 'Invitation sent' (packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts#invite_user), yet after Confirm the console showed no feedback while the sys_invitation and sys_email rows were written (objectstack-ai/objectui#11817). Score it FAIL and cite the card; do not re-file.
Expected FAIL on stock: Studio Publish gives no success confirmation — only the header flips to 'No drafts pending publish' (objectstack-ai/objectui#11807).
Expected FAIL on stock: inline edit shows '1 row modified · Save All (1)' after a click with no value change (objectstack-ai/objectui#11816) — negative[1].

Undo is scored only where a surface offers it today (record edit — records-forms.record-edit-undo). Its absence elsewhere is recorded in the evidence and is never a FAIL of this item: which writes should offer Undo is a product decision, not this item's oracle.

variants: record create — New form save on showcase_task
record inline edit — Edit inline → change Priority → save the row
bulk delete — select two rows → Delete in the selection bar → confirm
kanban move — drag a card Backlog → To Do (direct manipulation: the card in its new column IS the success feedback; a refused move must revert with an error)
declared record action — Mark Done on a task record (declared successMessage 'Task marked done.', examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts#MarkDoneAction)
param action dialog — Setup → Users → Invite User → Confirm (declared successMessage 'Invitation sent')
approval decision — Approvals inbox → Approve with a comment
import — Tasks → Import a two-row CSV → the result screen
Studio autosave — rename a field label in the scratch package
Studio publish — Publish the scratch package
Studio discard — Discard changes on a pending draft
settings save — Settings → Localization → save a value
steps: sign in as admin; keep a second context (or the REST API) open to read server truth independently of the UI

for each variant perform the write once, then within ~2 s capture a screenshot and the DOM of every feedback region — toasts ([data-sonner-toast]), role=status / role=alert regions, and the surface's own save indicator — recording the verbatim text, or its absence
for each variant read server-side whether the write landed (GET the record, the metadata item or the sys_ row) and record the request's status from the network log
repeat the record rows signed in as the member persona, on member-owned records
negative pass: (a) submit the create form with a required field empty, then again with a value that breaks a validation rule; (b) open an inline editor and leave it without changing the value
where a variant offers Undo (record edit), click it and read the record back

acceptance.clause: every write that landed server-side produced visible feedback on the surface that started it — a toast, an inline status, or (direct manipulation only) the item visibly in its new place
acceptance.verify: per variant, the captured feedback text is non-empty, or (kanban only) the card's column in the DOM matches the status the server read returns; pair every row with its step-3 server read
acceptance.evidence: per-variant table: variant · landed (y/n, request status) · feedback text verbatim or 'none' · screenshot

acceptance.clause: success feedback names what changed — the record, item or count — rather than a bare 'Success' or a machine name
acceptance.verify: read the captured text: it names the subject (record title, invitee email, package label, 'N created · M skipped'); a generic 'Done' / 'Success' or a raw snake_case name scores FAIL for that row

acceptance.clause: a declared successMessage is the text the user sees
acceptance.verify: for Mark Done and Invite User compare the toast text with the action's declared successMessage (examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts#MarkDoneAction, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts#invite_user)
acceptance.evidence: declared string vs shown string, per action

acceptance.clause: a refused write shows an error that says why — next to the field or in an error toast — and never a success message
acceptance.verify: negative (a): the request answers 4xx, the UI shows the server's reason, and no success toast appears in the same capture window
acceptance.evidence: request status and error code, the error text shown, screenshot

acceptance.clause: a no-op claims nothing — leaving an editor unchanged produces no saved/modified state and sends no write
acceptance.verify: negative (b): no PATCH/PUT in the network log and no modified or saved indicator in the DOM
acceptance.evidence: network log excerpt and DOM capture

acceptance.clause: where Undo is offered it restores the prior value server-side
acceptance.verify: after Undo, GET the record and compare the field with its pre-edit value

negative: a refused write (required field empty, validation rule broken) never shows a success toast
a no-op (open and close an inline editor without a change) produces no 'modified' state and no write request
feedback claiming success while the write did not land (4xx/5xx, or no request at all) is a FAIL — the inverse of a silent success
source: maintainer instruction, verbatim: 「写进测试清单：把这些原则加到 docs/qa/platform-checklist/，例如"每个写操作都有反馈""每个禁用控件都说明原因""不对用户显示机器名"。这样以后每轮测试都会检查。」

items.title: Every disabled control explains itself — the reason shows on hover and on keyboard focus, and is exposed as an accessible description
personas: member (non-admin) — for the disabled states only a non-privileged persona meets

requires: a showcase_task record with done = false (the stock seeds carry several)
the read-only showcase package in Studio (stock)
knownGaps: Expected FAIL on stock: the task record's Archive button (examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts#ArchiveTaskAction, disabled while has(record.done) && record.done != true) renders disabled in both its record_header and record_section placements with no title, tooltip or aria-describedby (objectstack-ai/objectui#11811). The action spec has no author-facing reason next to `disabled`, so a generic platform fallback passes clause 3 and is recorded as generic in the evidence — note which one was shown.
Known PASS reference: Studio's Publish button on the read-only showcase package carries a tooltip — check it first to calibrate the oracle before scoring the other rows.

variants: declared action disabled by its `disabled` predicate — Archive on a not-done task, record header AND record section placement
Studio Publish on a read-only package
Studio controls on a read-only package — the automation enable toggle, field inspector inputs, validation editor selects
import wizard — the step's continue/import button while a required field is unmapped
a form submit button, where the surface disables it instead of validating on submit
toolbar or bulk buttons rendered disabled for the member persona
steps: sign in as admin; on each variant locate every control rendered disabled (the disabled attribute, aria-disabled=true, or data-disabled)
hover each one for 1 s and screenshot; then reach it — or its focusable wrapper — with Tab and screenshot again
read the accessibility tree for each control: accessible name, accessible description (the aria-describedby target's text) and title
repeat the member-persona variant signed in as a member

acceptance.clause: every disabled control shows a reason on pointer hover
acceptance.verify: the hover screenshot shows a tooltip or adjacent text explaining the disabled state; nothing appearing scores FAIL for that control
acceptance.evidence: per-control screenshot with the control's label

acceptance.clause: the same reason is reachable without a pointer and exposed to assistive technology
acceptance.verify: the control or its focusable wrapper is in the tab order and carries an accessible description (aria-describedby resolving to non-empty text) or a title; a disabled control with neither scores FAIL

acceptance.clause: the reason is specific when the author or the platform knows the condition, generic only as a fallback
acceptance.verify: classify each reason: one that names the condition (e.g. 'Available once the task is done', 'This package is read-only') or a generic fallback ('Not available') passes, and the evidence records which of the two it was; an empty reason fails
acceptance.evidence: verbatim reason strings, classified specific / generic / none

negative: an ENABLED control carries no leftover disabled reason
a control removed by its `visible` predicate is absent from the DOM rather than rendered disabled — out of this item's scope; record it if seen

items.title: Where a label exists users see the label — machine names, raw ids and spec paths appear only as secondary text

requires: a writable scratch package for the Studio rows holding one object, one permission set and one nav item
read access to the served metadata of every sampled surface — labels are read from metadata, never assumed
knownGaps: Expected FAIL on stock: Explain access renders the principal as the raw user id; the Access list shows a new permission set by its name; the nav editor shows nav_item_N and truncated object names; the Changes panel lists machine names (objectstack-ai/objectui#11862).
Expected FAIL on stock: Profile shows the auth library's raw user.role ('user') for the platform admin (objectstack-ai/objectui#11866).
Expected FAIL on stock: the flow inspector's Node Type select lists raw snake_case types such as http_request, connector_action and try_catch (objectstack-ai/objectui#11778).
Regression rows, expected PASS: the audit-log actor and composite field values render as people and labels since objectstack-ai/objectui#11697.

variants: Studio → Access → Explain access result (the principal line)
Studio → Access → permission-set list (scratch package)
Studio → Interfaces → nav editor items (scratch package)
Studio → Changes panel (pending items)
Studio → flow inspector Node Type select
Studio → field type picker and the object pickers (Lookup related object, flow trigger object)
console → list column headers and the filter field picker (showcase_task)
console → record page lookup and user values (showcase_task)
Setup → audit log actor column
avatar menu → Profile (role badge and Role field)
error banners met while running the other items (Studio save refusals)
steps: before the browser: for each variant read the served metadata (GET /api/v1/meta/<type>/<name>) and note each sampled item's label next to its machine name — expectations derive from data
sign in as admin; visit each variant, screenshot it and capture the DOM text of each sampled item's primary label
for user references read the user's name and email (GET /api/v1/data/sys_user/<id>) and compare with what renders
scan the visible text of every variant for an id-shaped string (20+ alphanumeric characters), a dotted Zod path (segment.index.segment), a TypeScript class name, or an issue reference (repo#number)

acceptance.clause: the primary text of each sampled item is its label, not its machine name
acceptance.verify: compare the rendered primary text with the label and name read in step 1; rendered text equal to the name while a distinct label exists scores FAIL for that row
acceptance.evidence: per-row table: surface · label · name · rendered text

acceptance.clause: user references render as a person, never as an id
acceptance.verify: the rendered text equals the user's name or email from the sys_user read; an id-shaped string scores FAIL
acceptance.evidence: rendered string vs sys_user name / email

acceptance.clause: where a machine name is shown it is secondary — beside its label and visually subordinate
acceptance.verify: the machine name appears only next to its label, in smaller, muted or monospace text
acceptance.evidence: a screenshot per row where a machine name appears

acceptance.clause: user-facing banners and help text carry no raw spec path, class name or tracker id
acceptance.verify: no visible string on any variant matches a dotted Zod path, a TypeScript class name such as MetadataClient, or an issue reference
acceptance.evidence: every matching string, with its surface

negative: a machine name rendered because the item genuinely declares no label is an authoring gap, not a renderer FAIL — read the metadata before scoring
developer surfaces (the API panel, Advanced JSON editors) may show machine names — out of scope
